artifacts.summary: Nine-phase plan for the verified two-layer certificate wire codec: canonical JSON value and printer, total fuel parser, lexical and generic round-trip theorems, fuel sufficiency, schema codec with five contract theorems, envelope migration, and the echo plus joint-contract documentation. Nine theorems pinned in a Lean Challenge Statements block.

memory_candidates.content: Verified printer/parser round trips in Lean 4 factor cleanly into two layers, and the split is what makes the proof tractable. Layer 1: a generic canonical value type as MUTUAL inductives (never a nested `List T` field -- the induction hypothesis goes awkward), a `List Char`-valued canonical printer, and a fuel-indexed TOTAL `def` parser (never `partial def`, which yields no equation lemmas and so admits no theorem at all; never `partial_fixpoint`, which gives partial correctness only and leaves totality unestablished). Layer 2: a schema encode/decode pair over that value. The lexical work (escapes, digits, whitespace, arm overlap) is then proved once, generically, in the lemma shape `parse (print x ++ rest) = .ok (x, rest)`, and the schema theorem becomes pure structural induction with no parser state in it. Three load-bearing constraints: (a) no `do`-notation in any function the proof unfolds, because `do` desugars to `<$>`/`bind` which `simp` will not reduce; (b) print/parse integers through `Nat.digits`/`Nat.ofDigits` (`Nat.ofDigits_digits`), never `toString`/`String.toNat?`, for which no bridging lemma exists; (c) set the measure's empty cases to 0, or the fuel-sufficiency bound `size j <= (print j).length` fails at the empty-container leaf. Bridge `String` to `List Char` with `String.toList_append`, `String.toList_ofList`, `String.toList_injective`.
